svg.title: Name lookup and local echo replies.
svg.desc: Two independent examples show getent ahosts example.com with one illustrative address row and ping -c 3 127.0.0.1 with one illustrative reply. Documentation IP and timing are not promised actual results. RTT is the elapsed time for a request to reach the destination and its reply to return. Neither test proves HTTP works.
svg.text: LOOK UP NAMES, TEST ECHO REPLIES.
1. Name lookup: ask your Linux system for the name's addresses.
One illustrative row; actual addresses differ. /etc/hosts can supply local entries.
2. Independent local test: three echo requests to THIS computer.
64 bytes from 127.0.0.1: icmp_seq=1 ttl=64 time=0.04 ms
Illustrative reply. RTT = round-trip time: request out, reply back; ms = milliseconds.
Echo replies don't prove HTTP works; blocked echoes don't prove a site is down.
Requires getent and ping. Missing ping? See Package Management / 01–02.
